scenes.title: AI isn't magic.
scenes.narration: AI is not magic. It learns useful patterns from examples.

scenes.title: Start with examples.
scenes.narration: Imagine predicting ice cream sales from the temperature. Each dot is a day we have already seen.

scenes.title: Guess. Compare. Adjust.
scenes.narration: At first, our model guesses badly. Training compares its predictions with the real answers, then adjusts its numbers to make the errors smaller. Repeat that process, and a useful pattern starts to emerge.

scenes.title: Connections learn.
scenes.narration: Neural networks do this with many connected layers. The connections have strengths, called weights, that change during training.

scenes.title: Now try something new.
scenes.narration: Once trained, the model can make predictions about new examples. But a good fit to old data is not enough. Test it on new data.

scenes.title: A prediction
scenes.narration: And remember: a prediction can still be wrong.

prediction.title: One little token at a time

scenes.title: How does AI write?
scenes.narration: How does AI write a sentence? A language model predicts the next piece of text, called a token.

scenes.title: Words become tokens.
scenes.narration: A token might be a whole word, a word part, or punctuation. The text so far provides context.

scenes.title: Context changes the odds.
scenes.narration: After the cat sat on the, mat might be likely. Moon is possible, but less likely. These example probabilities are made up.

scenes.title: Predict. Add. Repeat.
scenes.narration: The system chooses a token, adds it to the sentence, and predicts again. Repeating this can produce a whole paragraph.

scenes.title: Turn up the surprise.
scenes.narration: A setting called temperature changes how varied the choices are. More variety does not mean more truth.

scenes.title: Sounds convincing?
scenes.narration: A fluent answer can still be wrong. Treat important answers as a starting point, and check the evidence.
